desc:
Subscription revenue, churn and MRR reports, built by Ecom Swift LLC. We turn your billing data into a short report that shows recurring revenue, new and lost customers, plan counts and failed payments, with each number explained in plain words.

## What is a subscription revenue report?

A subscription revenue report summarizes the health of recurring billing. Its core figure is monthly recurring revenue, often shortened to MRR, which is the amount your active subscriptions bring in each month. Around it sit the counts that explain movement: customers gained, customers lost, customers per plan and payments that failed.

The raw data already exists in your payment provider. The difficulty is that it is spread across customers, subscriptions, invoices and events, and each provider labels them differently. A report gathers these pieces, applies one clear definition per number and shows the result on a single page.

## Why founders need numbers they can trust

Without a report, decisions rest on feeling. A founder may think growth is steady while cancellations quietly rise, or may think pricing is fine while most customers sit on the cheapest plan. A short report makes these patterns visible early enough to act on them.

Trust in the numbers matters as much as the numbers themselves. If two people calculate churn differently, a meeting becomes an argument about method. Writing each definition down, and checking the figures against a sample of real customers, removes that argument. A report that refreshes by itself also saves the monthly ritual of exporting files and fixing formulas.

## What a useful report includes

- Monthly recurring revenue, shown with its change from the previous month.
- New customers and cancelled customers for each month.
- Customer churn and revenue churn, with the definition printed beside each.
- Customer counts by plan.
- Failed payment totals, so you can see how much revenue is at risk.
- Charts covering the last twelve months.
- Cohorts by sign-up month, showing how long customers stay.
- Revenue split by plan and by country.
- Trial to paid conversion, where you run trials.
- A written definitions page, so every figure has one meaning.

## How we build it

We begin by listing the questions you want answered, then map each one to data in your provider. We pull the data, build the calculations and compare the results with a hand-checked sample of customers to make sure they match. The Basic package delivers a one-page summary as a spreadsheet, with MRR, new and cancelled customers and counts by plan. The Standard package adds trend charts, churn rates and failed payment totals, and places the report on a page inside your app, together with written definitions. The Premium package adds cohort charts, revenue by plan and country, trial conversion and a weekly summary email to your team, followed by a handover call.

You choose the format that suits you: a spreadsheet you open, a page in your app, or a scheduled email. We read data from your provider with limited, read-only access where the provider supports it. The report describes what has happened. It does not forecast the future unless you add a forecast sheet, and Ecom Swift LLC cannot promise any particular growth outcome.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which five or six numbers matter most before building charts.
- Write one definition for each metric and keep it unchanged.
- Check the first report against a few real customers by hand.
- Review the report on the same day each month or week.
- Track failed payments alongside cancellations.

**Avoid:**
- Counting trial users or test accounts as paying customers.
- Mixing monthly and yearly plans without converting them to a monthly figure.
- Comparing months using different definitions.
- Filling the page with every metric the provider can produce.
- Sharing an unchecked report with investors or partners.

## Who this is for

This service suits a founder who exports files every month and rebuilds the same spreadsheet. It suits a small team that wants a weekly summary without hiring an analyst. It also suits a company preparing for a funding conversation that needs clean subscription figures.

## What we need from you

Tell us which billing provider you use, which questions you want the report to answer and how you want to receive it. If you run trials, coupons or multiple currencies, mention them so we count them correctly. We need read access or a team role in your provider account and developer access if the report lives in your app. We never need passwords. After you order, you receive a checklist and a first draft to review.
